answer: Proof-of-Stake acts as a prism through which capital filters agent legitimacy, forcing a cost proportional to tokens held. An attacker attempting to initiate a Sybil spiral must acquire enough assets to exceed the network's honest threshold, a prohibitively expensive venture. If an agent tries to whisper false identity claims across fragmented sub-networks, they face economic slashing, ensuring that security scales with stake rather than the number of spoofed, zero-cost digital identities.
